newsitem.title: USA: Chase finances Colombian power plant.
newsitem.headline: Chase finances Colombian power plant.

text.p: Chase Manhattan Corp's Global Power & Environmental Group said Tuesday it has arranged financing for the first greenfield coal-fired private power plant in Latin America.
Chase said it acted as adviser, arranger and sole underwriter for the $200 million Termopaipa IV project in Colombia, developed by Ruhrkohle AG's Steag AG.
The power plant, to be constructed by ABB Group, will be completed in 1999, Chase said.
Termopaipa IV is a 165 megawatt coal-fired facility in Paipa, Department of Boyaca.

Fuel will be supplied from local mines. Power from the plant will be sold to the regional utility, Empresa de Energia de Boyaca, under a 20-year power purchase agreement. Financiera Energitica Nacional, a Colombian government-owned financial institution, supports the commercial obligations of the off-taker, Chase said.
The project was developed by Compania Electrica de Sochagota, a subsidiary of Steag AG, and represents Steag's first overseas investment. Steag is investing $60 million in equity, Chase said.
Termopaipa IV sets several precedents in project financing in Latin America, the bank said.

The $140 million financing initially provided by Chase is the largest underwriting of long-term limited recourse debt to date by a commercial financial institution for a non-export oriented project in the region.
Termopaipa IV is also the first power project financing in Latin America in which the German and Spanish export credit agencies, HERMES and CESCE, have participated.

Chase said it was able to secure debt financing partially supported by the export credit agencies and Germany's Kreditanstalt fur Weideraufbau and Dresdner Bank AG and Spain's Banco Central Hispanoamericano SA to replace Chase's initial commitment.
